chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, and Hammad, from Al-Halby, all together, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding
a man who pelts the Jamarah in reverse order. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should repeat upon Al-Wusta (the middle), and Jamarat Al-Aqabah.'

key_terms.الْجِمَارَ: The stone pillars in Mina used for the ritual of stoning the devil during Hajj.
key_terms.الْوُسْطَى: The middle pillar among the three Jamarat pillars.
key_terms.جَمْرَةِ الْعَقَبَةِ: The final and largest of the three Jamarat pillars, located closest to Mecca.
key_terms.مَنْكُوسَةً: In reverse order or upside down; referring to throwing stones out of the prescribed sequence.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim stones the Jamarat pillars in the wrong order during Hajj?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the specific fiqh of Hajj rituals, emphasizing the importance of maintaining the prescribed sequence (tartib) during the stoning of the Jamarat. It highlights the scholarly principle that deviations in ritual order require specific corrective actions rather than a complete repetition, reflecting the precision valued in Shia jurisprudence. The hadith underscores the continuity of prophetic tradition as transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt, ensuring the validity of the pilgrim's worship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, and Hammad, from Al Halby, altogether, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding
a man who pelts the Jamarah (in the reverse order). Heasws said: ‘He should repeat upon Al-Wusta (the middle), and Jamarah’ Al-Aqabah.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar and Hammad from al-Halabiy who all have said the following: “This is about
a man who reversed the order of throwing pebbles. Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’He must throw pebbles on al-Wusta, then on Jamarah al-‘AqabahY”
